Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
2. Heard Sri Birendra Singh Khokher, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri R.P Patel, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3. This is the second bail application on behalf of the applicant.
The first one was rejected by this Court vide order dated 18.01.2023.
4. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.024 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 304-B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Sector- New Agra, District Agra, during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Manish Kumar vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the applicant was married to the deceased as per Hindu rites on 08.11.2019.

The applicant along with his mother is stated to have subjected her to cruelty for demand of dowry and leading her to death on 09.01.2020 at about 04:00 P.M.
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
There are several transcription of the conversations between the parties which indicates that applicant was having cordial relations with the deceased.
Learned counsel further stated that ingredients of Section 304-B IPC are not fulfilled as there is no particular allegation of demand of dowry before her death.
The cause of death of the deceased has been found to be asphyxia as a result of hanging and it is suicidal death.
Learned counsel has stated that mother of applicant has already been enlarged on bail by this Court.

Learned counsel further stated that the period of four years and about two months has already been passed since the arrest of the applicant and charge could be framed on 04.03.2023 and only the examination-in-chief of PW-1 has been recorded.
There is no likelihood of conclusion of trial in near future as the trial is moving at a snails pace.
Learned counsel has stated that fundamental rights of the applicant enshrined under article 21 of the Constitution of India stand violated.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 14.01.2020.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

8. The Apex Court in the case of Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712, has observed as under:-
"We are conscious of the fact that the charges levelled against the respondent are grave and a serious threat to societal harmony.

entities.text: Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Had it been a case at the threshold,
we would have outrightly turned down the respondent's prayer.

However, keeping in mind the length of the period spent by him in custody and the unlikelihood of the trial being completed anytime soon, the High Court appears to have been left with no other option except to grant bail."

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, period of custody and the fact that the trial is moving at snail pace and also taking into consideration the judgments of Apex Court passed in the case of K.A. Najeeb (supra) and Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant- Manish Kumar involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.

Manish Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126463714/
2 (ii).

entities.text: Manish Kumar vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
11.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witness.
